reason: The only offered action assembles an instrument to examine the sky.
expectation: I expect a telescope that can be used to observe the Moon, Jupiter and Venus.

effect: The telescope is ready for the three observations, whose interpretation will need comparison.
reaction: The instrument assembly was straightforward; I’m curious what the observations will show.
reason: The changing Moon shadows provide a direct way to examine whether its surface is smooth.
expectation: I expect the shadows to support a rough lunar surface, though their interpretation may need comparison.

alternatives.reason: Jupiter’s nearby points could test whether everything circles Earth, but I’ll examine the Moon first.

effect: The Moon’s shadows support a rough surface and challenge a strict distinction between Earth and the heavens.
reaction: The comparison with earthly shadows made the inference clear.
reason: Observing Jupiter’s nearby points addresses whether everything must circle Earth.
expectation: I expect their changing positions to suggest that they orbit Jupiter, though repeated observations may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Venus’s phases are also a goal, but I’ll examine Jupiter first.

effect: Jupiter’s moons show that not everything orbits Earth directly, but they do not establish that Earth moves.
reaction: The distinction between those two claims is useful.
reason: The only offered combination addresses the remaining goal of observing Venus’s phases.
expectation: I expect observations over several months to reveal Venus’s changing phases and possibly constrain sky models.

effect: Venus’s full range of phases gives sky models another observation to account for; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The result is clear, though I would have liked to see how the phases distinguish competing models.

mostWorthwhile.text: Jupiter’s moons were most worthwhile: they challenge the claim that everything circles Earth directly without pretending to prove that Earth moves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the telescope was straightforward, but as the only offered action it involved little decision-making.

surprise.text: The distinction between Jupiter’s moons orbiting Jupiter and proof that Earth moves sharpened my understanding of what the observation establishes.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the telescope assembly was a predictable prerequisite.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how Venus’s phases and the other observations test competing sky models, particularly since this chapter stopped short of comparing them.
